principles: Current product identity in user-facing CLI output should say Lattice, not Koala.
Legacy compatibility identifiers must remain stable when they are consumed by existing users or lifecycle gates.
Generated dist output must come from the TypeScript build, not manual edits.
Claude CLI participation must be visible as evidence, not only implied by conversation.
drivers: User reported visible Koala remnants in CLI-engine output after package rename.
Reviewer lanes and legacy aliases still depend on some koala-prefixed tokens.
The change touches CLI help/diagnostics and process-adjacent strings, so verification must include scan and build checks.

options.name: A: Classified cleanup with legacy allowlist
pros: Removes current-product Koala branding while preserving stable compatibility contracts.
Produces an auditable list of remaining legacy tokens.
Matches the user request without risking reviewer lane or alias breakage.
cons: Some koala strings will intentionally remain, so verification must classify them instead of expecting zero hits.

options.name: B: Blind global Koala to Lattice replacement
pros: Fastest apparent cleanup and likely reduces raw grep count most aggressively.
cons: Could break koala command alias, koala.config.json fallback, .koala legacy paths, koala-codex detection, and koala-review-* process gates.

options.name: C: Documentation-only explanation of residuals
pros: Lowest code risk and preserves all compatibility behavior.
cons: Does not satisfy the user-visible cleanup request because cli-engine help and diagnostics would still present Koala as current product identity.

chosen: A: Classified cleanup with legacy allowlist
rationale: Choose classified cleanup because it is the only option that both fixes user-visible product identity and protects lifecycle/runtime compatibility contracts. The implementation will rename current-product wording, label remaining koala tokens as legacy where visible, and add a focused scan so future changes cannot reintroduce unclassified Koala branding.

preMortem.scenario: Reviewer lane names are renamed accidentally
preMortem.trigger: A broad replace changes koala-review-* tokens in cli-engine or related process files.
preMortem.consequence: REVIEW/DONE gates cannot match signed reviewer evidence or process fact contract checks fail.
preMortem.mitigation: Treat koala-review-* as allowlisted legacy/process contract and verify with process fact contract checks.

preMortem.trigger: The cleanup removes koala alias wording or koala.config.json fallback handling instead of labeling it legacy.
preMortem.consequence: Existing users with old command/config paths get broken behavior or confusing diagnostics.
preMortem.mitigation: Preserve legacy command/config/path tokens and ensure visible text says legacy alias/fallback.

preMortem.trigger: Generated packages/main/dist/cli-engine.js is manually edited or not regenerated after TypeScript changes.
preMortem.consequence: Runtime CLI output still differs from source or build overwrites the cleanup later.
preMortem.mitigation: Edit src only, run npm --prefix packages/main run build, and scan both src and dist.
